<!--
No fixed sections. Use headings that fit this change — the merged pull requests
are the guide, and the ones worth copying name their own structure ("The
evidence", "Why removing it loses nothing") instead of filling a skeleton.

Whatever the shape, a reader should come away knowing what the change does and
how you know it works. The last is not "CI is green" — it is the measurement,
the limit, or the break you made to confirm a new test can fail at all.

Keep the two kinds of "not done here" under separate headings. A settled
decision (an accepted cost, a scope chosen against) states its cost and implies
no further work, e.g. under "Decisions and their cost". Open work the change
knowingly leaves links each item to its issue, e.g. under "Follow-ups". One
heading for both makes every decision read as owed work.

The squash commit takes the COMMIT messages, not this description, so the two
are written for different readers and neither has to serve both.

The commit convention, changesets and the Eclipse Contributor Agreement are in
CONTRIBUTING.md.
-->
